stories.headline: US launches Operation Economic Outcast to isolate Iran with sweeping sanctions
stories.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a major sanctions campaign against Iran on August 24, 2026. President Donald Trump directed the launch of Operation Economic Outcast. The operation targets Iran and its foreign enablers. Bessent said the objective is to cut off every economic lifeline that sustains the Iranian regime. He said Tehran must be left standing completely alone.

Bessent announced an unprecedented global economic war against all Iranian revenue streams. The effort directly targets Iran's oil revenue. He named five key sectors supporting the Iranian economy. These sectors are digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping. They will all face heightened scrutiny from the United States. Bessent warned that any entity helping Iran wash money will face strict penalties. They will be removed from the US dollar financial system.

Bessent said Trump is personally calling world leaders. Trump is asking them to stop all economic dealings with Tehran. Bessent pointed to recent actions by the United Arab Emirates as proof of diplomatic success. The country suspended trade, commercial exchanges, and financial transactions with Iran.

Iran warned it would stop all regional oil exports if the conflict with the US continues. The regime also warned ships not to cross the Strait of Hormuz without permission. Economist David Oxley said about 90% of Iran's oil exports go to China. Oxley works as chief climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics. On August 24, 2026, Brent crude oil reached $92 per barrel. Gasoline prices in the United States went over $4 per gallon.

The US dollar index rose 0.17 percent to 98.99 on August 24, 2026. This increase came after the US announced expanded sanctions. CNBC reported that Bessent could use the Treasury General Account. The account holds near $1 trillion at the Federal Reserve. He could use it to fund bond buybacks.

The market actions also affected Canada. The Canadian dollar fell 0.61 percent to C$1.385 per US dollar on August 24, 2026. Trump threatened to raise tariffs on Canadian goods to 50% on January 1, 2027. These goods include cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said this threat was expected. Carney asked what message it sends to US workers who rely on Canadian demand. He mentioned workers in states like Michigan and Ohio.

Public support for the war has dropped among Americans. A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed support fell to 31%. This was down from 34% earlier in August 2026. Among Republicans, 69% support the war with Iran. That is down from 77% in March. Recent polling showed Trump's approval rating at a low of 33%.

claims.text: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced on August 24, 2026, that the United States Treasury has launched Operation Economic Outcast against Iran and its enablers at the direction of Donald Trump.
Scott Bessent stated that the objective of Operation Economic Outcast is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains the Iranian regime until Tehran stands alone.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced an unprecedented global economic war targeting all of Iran's revenue streams, including oil.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent identified digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping as five critical sectors supporting Iran's economy that will face heightened scrutiny.
Scott Bessent warned that any entity facilitating money laundering on behalf of Iran will be removed from the US dollar-based financial system.
Scott Bessent stated that President Donald Trump is personally contacting world leaders to ask them to stop economic interactions with Tehran.
Scott Bessent cited the United Arab Emirates' decision to suspend trade, commercial exchanges, and financial transactions with Iran as evidence of success from US diplomatic efforts.
Iran warned it would halt all regional oil exports if the conflict with the United States continues.
The Iranian regime warned maritime traffic not to navigate through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission.
Capital Economics chief climate and commodities economist David Oxley noted that approximately 90% of Iran's oil exports go to China.
On August 24, 2026, the price of Brent crude oil reached $92 per barrel.
Gasoline prices in the United States surpassed $4 per gallon.
The US dollar index rose 0.17 percent to 98.99 on August 24, 2026, following the announcement of expanded sanctions on Iran.
CNBC reported that US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could use the Treasury General Account at the Federal Reserve, which holds near $1 trillion, to fund bond buybacks.
The Canadian dollar weakened 0.61 percent to C$1.385 per US dollar on August 24, 2026.
Donald Trump threatened to increase tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel to 50% starting January 1, 2027.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Donald Trump's new tariff threat was largely expected and questioned what message it sends to US workers in states like Michigan and Ohio who rely on Canadian demand.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed public support for the war with Iran among Americans surveyed dropped to 31%, down from 34% earlier in August 2026.
The Reuters/Ipsos poll indicated that 69% of Republican respondents support the war with Iran, down from 77% in March.
Donald Trump's approval rating hovered at a low of 33% according to recent polling.

stories.headline: US-Canada trade negotiations collapse as Trump threatens 50 percent auto tariffs
stories.body:
Trade negotiations between the United States and Canada collapsed after both sides failed to reach an agreement. Donald Trump announced a 50% tariff on Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel. The new tax starts on January 1, 2027.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended negotiations and recalled his team to Ottawa. Carney said Canada rejected the US terms because of last-minute demands. He said those demands limited tariff relief and restricted Canada's trade independence. Carney said Canada will return to talks only when the US acts like a true partner. An Angus Reid Institute poll showed three in four Canadians supported his decision to walk away.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford said Trump declared economic war on Canada. Ford warned Canada could cut off electricity and critical minerals to the US. Industry leader Flavio Volpe warned that tariffs on auto parts would stop US car assembly.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the US had to act after Canadian retaliation. Annual trade between the two nations reached about $909 billion. On August 24, shares of Ford fell 3.2%, Stellantis fell 4.7%, and General Motors fell 1.1%. Trump claimed on Truth Social that Canadian farm tariffs created a $60 billion trade deficit.

claims.text: Trade negotiations between the United States and Canada collapsed after the two nations failed to reach an agreement.
Donald Trump announced a new 50% tariff on Canadian automobiles, trucks, auto parts, and steel set to take effect on January 1, 2027.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended trade negotiations with the US and recalled Canada's negotiating team back to Ottawa.
Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canada rejected proposed US terms because the US added last-minute demands that limited tariff relief and restricted Canada's trade independence.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada will return to the negotiating table only when the US approaches talks with a true partnership attitude.
An Angus Reid Institute poll found that three in four Canadians supported Prime Minister Mark Carney's decision to walk away from trade negotiations with the US.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford stated that US President Donald Trump had declared economic war against Canada.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford warned that Canada could cut off electricity and critical mineral supplies to the United States as leverage in the trade dispute.
Flavio Volpe, president of Canada's Automotive Parts Manufacturers' Association, warned that US tariffs on Canadian auto parts would halt auto assembly across the United States.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that the United States was compelled to take countermeasures following Canadian retaliation against US exports.
According to the Office of the US Trade Representative, annual trade between the United States and Canada reached roughly $909 billion.
Following the trade announcement on August 24, shares of Ford fell 3.2%, Stellantis fell 4.7%, and General Motors fell 1.1%.
Donald Trump claimed on Truth Social that Canadian agricultural tariffs contributed to a $60 billion trade deficit between the United States and Canada.

stories.headline: Britain expands Ukraine military support with missile technology and AI partnership
stories.body:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Kyiv on August 24, 2026. This was his first official trip abroad as prime minister. Burnham and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a new defense AI partnership. Britain became the first foreign partner to access Ukraine's Avengers AI Labs.

The deal allows the UK to use AI models trained on Ukrainian battlefield data. This technology will protect British military sites and infrastructure. The Avengers database contains 5 million battlefield images from the DELTA combat management system. These AI systems analyze over 100,000 drone video feeds monthly and spot about 70 percent of targets in real time. Burnham said this work will speed up security efforts. The UK Ministry of Defence approved AI projects with British tech companies Sintela, Mind Foundry, and Skyral.

The UK also allowed defense firm MBDA to share declassified details on Scalp cruise missiles. This enables Ukraine to make missile components locally. The missile measures 5.10 metres long and weighs about 1,300 kg. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the transfer undermines peace efforts. He said Russian forces are searching for production sites.

Britain has given over £25 billion in military and civilian help to Ukraine since 2022. Meanwhile, the European Union released €6.1 billion in military aid. Former intelligence officer Dr. Frank Ledwidge said European commitments fail to solve Kyiv's need for air defence interceptors.

claims.text: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Kyiv on August 24, 2026, marking his first official trip abroad as prime minister.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a defence AI partnership, making Britain the first international partner to access Ukraine's Avengers AI Labs.
The United Kingdom and Ukraine established a deal to use AI models trained on Ukrainian battlefield data from the Avengers AI lab to protect British infrastructure and military sites.
Ukraine's Avengers AI Labs database contains 5 million annotated battlefield images largely collected from the DELTA combat management system.
AI systems trained on Avengers Labs data analyze over 100,000 drone video feeds monthly and identify approximately 70 percent of targets in real time.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that combining British AI expertise with Ukrainian battlefield data will accelerate capabilities to protect national security.
The UK Ministry of Defence approved pilot AI projects with British technology companies Sintela, Mind Foundry, and Skyral.
The UK government authorized defense company MBDA to declassify information on British components of the Scalp cruise missile to enable domestic production in Ukraine.
The Storm Shadow/Scalp cruise missile measures 5.10 metres in length and weighs approximately 1,300 kg.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov condemned the UK's transfer of missile component technology, stating it undermines peace efforts and that Russian forces are actively locating target production sites.
The UK government has committed more than £25 billion ($34 billion) in military and civilian assistance to Ukraine since 2022.
The European Union released €6.1 billion (£5.2 billion) in military aid to Ukraine as part of a total €90 billion loan facility.

Former military intelligence officer Dr. Frank Ledwidge stated that recent European commitments to Ukraine are politically symbolic and fail to address Kyiv's primary need for air defence interceptors.

stories.headline: US Department of Homeland Security proposes 103,265 dollar H-1B visa fee
stories.body:
The US Department of Homeland Security published a new rule in the Federal Register on Monday. The rule proposes a new $103,265 fee for cap-subject H-1B visa petitions. This proposal opens a 30-day public comment period. Officials could finalize the new rule by the end of 2026.

The H-1B program allows American employers to hire foreign workers for specialty jobs. The visa lasts up to three years initially. It can be extended up to six years total. The government sets an annual cap of 85,000 new visas. This total includes 65,000 regular visas and 20,000 visas reserved under the Master's cap. US Citizenship and Immigration Services already received enough petitions to reach both caps for fiscal year 2027.

The proposed $103,265 charge is an extra payment. It comes on top of existing filing fees and statutory costs. Before recent increases, government fees for H-1B visas usually ranged from $2,000 to $5,000. In August, officials introduced extra fees of up to $4,500 for extension or transfer requests.

An earlier $100,000 fee was introduced in September 2025 through a presidential proclamation. That fee expires in September 2026 unless extended. However, legal battles have blocked that requirement. On June 8, 2026, a federal judge in Massachusetts struck down guidance implementing the $100,000 fee. On July 24, 2026, an appeals court refused to pause that ruling. As of February 15, only 70 employers had paid the $100,000 fee for 85 workers.

Legal expert Mitch Wexler said the proposed $103,265 fee depends on whether a petition is cap-subject, not worker location. Higher education institutions and affiliated non-profit groups will not pay the fee. Research organizations are also exempt. New York immigration lawyer Cyrus D Mehta called the fee preposterous. He said the government killed the goose that laid the golden eggs.

Government officials estimate the fee will raise $8.78 billion each year. They estimate 14,541 small businesses will be affected. For 76% of those businesses, costs will rise by more than 1% of annual revenue.

Indian workers rely heavily on the program. In fiscal year 2025, Indian citizens received 283,000 H-1B visas including extensions. That was 70% of all visas given. Indian workers also got nearly 58,000 new visas for initial employment.

Overall interest in the program has dropped. Employers registered for about 344,000 visas last year. That was down over 25 percent from 2024. It was far below the 794,000 registrations in 2023. Boundless Immigration CEO Xiao Wang said top sponsors now include Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Google. Company data showed senior Level III candidates had a 68% selection rate in March 2026. Entry-level Level I candidates had a 40% rate.

Lawmakers have also introduced the End H-1B Visa Abuse Act of 2026. It proposes a three-year pause on new visas, a cap of 25,000, and a $200,000 minimum salary threshold.

claims.text: The US Department of Homeland Security published the proposed $103,265 H-1B visa fee rule in the Federal Register on Monday, opening a 30-day public comment period.
The Trump administration proposed a new $103,265 fee for cap-subject H-1B petitions.
The US Department of Homeland Security could finalize the proposed H-1B fee regulation by the end of 2026.
The H-1B program allows US employers to hire foreign workers in specialty occupations for an initial period of up to three years, extendable up to six years.
The annual statutory cap for new H-1B visas is 85,000, which includes 65,000 regular visas and 20,000 visas reserved under the Master's cap.
US Citizenship and Immigration Services has already received enough petitions to reach the 65,000 regular cap and 20,000 master's cap for fiscal year 2027.
The US Department of Homeland Security proposed the new $103,265 fee as an additional charge on top of existing H-1B filing and statutory fees.
H-1B visa application government fees typically ranged from $2,000 to $5,000 prior to recent fee increases.
In August, the US Department of Homeland Security introduced additional fees of up to $4,500 for applications to extend H-1B stays or transfer overseas employees to the US.
A previous $100,000 H-1B payment introduced under a September 2025 presidential proclamation is set to expire in September 2026 unless extended.
On June 8, 2026, the US District Court for the District of Massachusetts vacated agency guidance implementing the $100,000 H-1B fee requirement in State of California v. Mullin.
On July 24, 2026, the US Court of Appeals for the First Circuit rejected the Trump administration's request to stay the District Court ruling against the $100,000 fee.
US Citizenship and Immigration Services received only 85 payments of the $100,000 fee from 70 employers as of February 15.

Mitch Wexler, senior counsel at Fragomen, stated that the proposed $103,265 fee is tied to whether an H-1B petition is cap-subject rather than whether the worker is physically inside or outside the US.
Higher education institutions, affiliated non-profits, and research organizations are eligible to hire cap-exempt H-1B workers without paying cap-subject fees.
New York-based immigration attorney Cyrus D Mehta called the proposed $103,265 fee preposterous and stated that the Trump administration has killed the goose that laid the golden eggs.
The US Department of Homeland Security estimates the proposed $103,265 fee would generate approximately $8.78 billion annually based on 85,000 cap-subject petitions.
The US Department of Homeland Security estimates 14,541 small entities would be affected by the proposed fee, with 76% facing cost increases exceeding 1% of annual revenue.
Indian nationals received 283,000 H-1B visas, including extensions, in the fiscal year ended 2025, representing 70% of the total allotted.
Indian nationals received nearly 58,000 new H-1B visas for initial employment in the fiscal year ended 2025.
Employers registered for about 344,000 H-1B visas last year, representing a decline of over 25 percent from 2024 and down from 794,000 in 2023.
According to Boundless Immigration CEO Xiao Wang, top H-1B sponsors in fiscal year 2025 shifted to companies including Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Google.
Boundless Immigration client data showed senior Level III candidates achieved a 68% selection rate in the March 2026 H-1B cap season compared to 40% for entry-level Level I candidates.
The proposed End H-1B Visa Abuse Act of 2026 proposes a three-year pause on new H-1B visas, a reduction of the annual cap to 25,000, and a minimum annual salary threshold of $200,000.
